original_question: Does FRT^2_2(Σ_n+1) imply FRT^3_2(Σ_n+1)? Here FRT^e_k(Σ_n+1) says that for any x there is a y such that every Σ_n+1 coloring C : [y]^e -> k has a homogeneous set H with |H| >= x.
target_in_paper: Section 5 (Wei Wang), Problem 12, second subquestion: "FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}) ⊢ FRT^3_2(Σ_{n+1})?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It captures the second half of Problem 12 in Section 5, keeps the same narrow scope (2 colors, pairs versus triples), and correctly states the intended finite Ramsey scheme FRT^e_k(Σ_{n+1}) as a bounded-size homogeneous-set principle for Σ_{n+1}-definable colorings on finite domains.
missing_details: The paper states this as an implication between principles/schemes, so a stand-alone version should specify the ambient proof-theoretic base. In the surrounding context, the comparison is carried out over IΣ_n, although the second half of Problem 12 leaves that base implicit.
n should be treated as a fixed natural index for the fragment IΣ_n and for the formula class Σ_{n+1}.
[y]^e should be spelled out as the set of e-element subsets of the initial segment {0,...,y-1}.
A "Σ_{n+1} coloring" should be made explicit as a k-valued function C:[y]^e -> k whose graph is Σ_{n+1}-definable in first-order arithmetic.
"Homogeneous" should be defined explicitly as: C is constant on [H]^e for some H subseteq {0,...,y-1} with |H| >= x.
The numerals e=2,3 and k=2 are fixed standard parameters here, not variables ranging over arbitrary exponents or numbers of colors.
refined_question: For each fixed n >= 0, working over the ambient fragment IΣ_n used in the surrounding discussion of Section 5, does FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}) imply FRT^3_2(Σ_{n+1})? Here FRT^e_k(Σ_{n+1}) is the scheme asserting that for every natural number x there exists y such that every Σ_{n+1}-definable coloring C:[{0,...,y-1}]^e -> k has a homogeneous set H subseteq {0,...,y-1} with |H| >= x, i.e. C is constant on [H]^e.
justification: The nearest official formulation in arXiv:2507.03972 is the second question in Problem 12 of Section 5. I kept exactly that target and only unpacked the notation that is defined immediately above Problem 12. I did not broaden the question to other Ramsey exponents, other numbers of colors, or neighboring principles such as WPHP, GPHP, or CARD. Because this paper is an open-problems list, there is no numbered equivalent reformulation of this particular implication in the paper itself; the only implicit point that needed to be made explicit for a stand-alone question is the surrounding base-theory setting over IΣ_n.
